headline: UltraDEX's listings are strong and well reviewed, but it advertises on almost none of its biggest searches, and a competitor is buying the ad slot on its own brand name.

points.title: Put ad support behind the big searches where UltraDEX already ranks
points.detail: Only 1 of the top 30 keywords across the best-sellers has an UltraDEX ad. The Fresh Breath Spray ranks #6 organically for 'bad breath' (73.6k/mo) with no ad, and the rinses sit at #39 for 'mouth wash' (24.7k/mo) and #49 for 'bad breath'. Exact-match ads on these terms are the fastest visibility win.
evidence: Sponsored coverage: 1 of top 30 keywords (Jungle Scout keywords by ASIN)
bad breath: 73,603/mo; Spray organic #6, Fluoride Rinse organic #49, no sponsored rank
mouth wash: 24,719/mo; Fluoride Rinse organic #39, no sponsored rank
toothpaste: 392,821/mo; Low-Abrasion Toothpaste organic #47, no sponsored rank, CPC ~£0.49

points.title: Defend the UltraDEX brand searches from CB12
points.detail: CB12 Mouthwash takes a sponsored slot at #4 on 'ultradex' and #15 on 'ultradex mouthwash', and UltraDEX runs no ads on its own name. Brand-term ads are cheap and keep loyal buyers from switching.
evidence: 'ultradex': CB12 Mouthwash sponsored at position 4 (DataForSEO, Amazon UK)
No UltraDEX sponsored placement on either brand search

points.title: Fresh Breath Spray: check the price and sellers
points.detail: The spray family (~£13–17k/mo) sells at £2.35 against a £7.16 list price (67% off) with 8 sellers on the listing. If the discount isn't planned, it's resellers driving the price down on one of the brand's top three products.
evidence: ~5,400 units/mo; Keepa cross-check ~£16.9k/mo for the family

points.title: Bring the multipacks into their product families
points.detail: Pack sizes are listed separately from their main products, e.g. the Fresh Breath Spray 12-pack, '6 x Daily Oral Rinse 250ml' and the toothpaste 6-packs. That splits reviews and sales rank across six sets of duplicate listings. Merging them into variation families pools both.
evidence: 6 duplicate groups among live listings (title match, different parents)
e.g. B016KXU6OK '6 x UltraDex Daily Oral Rinse 250ml' separate from the rinse family

points.title: 12hr Low-Abrasion Toothpaste: finish the listing
points.detail: This newer best-seller family (~£7–8k/mo, 57 reviews) has 5 images, no video and no A+, and its title cuts off on mobile before the pack size. Bringing it up to the standard of the rinses would help it convert.
evidence: Title cut off before the size in mobile search (first 80 characters)

hero_actions.B071VT9KBZ: Add ads on 'alcohol free mouthwash' (3.1k/mo, organic #43).
hero_actions.B007Y5XCZE: Exact-match ads on 'mouth wash' and 'bad breath'; drop 'otrivine' (sponsored #1, unrelated).
hero_actions.B007Y5XD3A: Test ads on 'toothpaste' and 'whitening toothpaste', where it ranks #47–48 with no ad support.
hero_actions.B00HIXUCNC: Back the #6 organic rank on 'bad breath' with ads; check the 67% discount and the 8 sellers.
hero_actions.B071Z1B158: Fold the 250ml 6-pack and 1L into the rinse families; add ads on 'fluoride mouth rinse'.
hero_actions.B0BG66FF4T: Add video and A+, a 6th and 7th image, and move the pack size into the first 80 characters of the title.

content_note: The rinses and the spray are well built for mobile (2000px zoomable images, brand videos, phone-friendly A+). The newer 12hr toothpaste is the gap.
ad_strategy_summary: UltraDEX is almost absent from paid search on its biggest terms. Defend the brand name first, then add exact-match ads where products already rank on page 1–3 ('bad breath', 'mouth wash', 'toothpaste').
amc_hypotheses: Most best-sellers offer Subscribe & Save in a repeat-purchase category, so repeat buyers are likely a large share of rinse and spray revenue.
With CB12 advertising on the brand name, some existing UltraDEX buyers are probably being tempted to switch at the point of reordering.
amc_questions: How many rinse buyers reorder, and after how many days?
Do spray buyers go on to buy the rinse or toothpaste?
How many shoppers who search 'ultradex' end up buying CB12?
